findings.title: Options-object calls enable rejectOnClear by default, contradicting the public default
findings.cause: When the constructor receives an options object, destructuring defaults `rejectOnClear` to `true` even though the variable is initialized to `false` and the documented default is `false`.
findings.impact: Callers using `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` get opt-in rejection semantics without opting in. `clearQueue()` rejects every pending promise with `AbortError`, which can break teardown paths and `Promise.all` users expecting the documented default behavior.
evidence: index.js:4 initializes `rejectOnClear` to false, but index.js:7 destructures `{concurrency, rejectOnClear = true}` for options objects.
index.js:77-89 rejects queued promises when `rejectOnClear` is true.
readme.md:46-50 and index.d.ts:101-106 document `rejectOnClear` as a boolean with default false.

Focused probe output for `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, queue one pending task, then `clearQueue()`: {"pendingCount":0,"outcome":{"status":"rejected","name":"AbortError","message":"This operation was aborted"}}.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 50))); const pending = limit(() => Promise.resolve('pending-ran')); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); console.log(await Promise.race([pending.then(v => ({status: 'fulfilled', v}), e => ({status: 'rejected', name: e?.name, message: e?.message})), new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve({status: 'still-pending'}), 20))])); await running;"

findings.title: limitFunction drops every argument passed to the limited wrapper
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is a zero-argument arrow that calls `function_()` instead of forwarding `...arguments_`.
findings.impact: Any consumer using `limitFunction(fn, options)` with a parameterized function receives `undefined` arguments at runtime. This violates the TypeScript contract and even breaks the repository benchmark path that calls `limitedTask(delay, i)`.
evidence: index.js:121-124 returns `() => limit(() => function_())`, so no caller arguments are captured.
index.d.ts:133-136 declares that the returned function accepts `(...arguments_: Arguments)`.
index.test-d.ts:25 type-checks `lf('input')`, but the runtime test only covers a no-argument limited function.
benchmark.js:193-194 calls a `limitFunction` wrapper with `(delay, i)`, which the implementation discards.
Focused probe output for `limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1})('kept')`: `undefined`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import {limitFunction} from './index.js'; const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited('kept'));"

findings.title: limit.map omits mapper indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The map implementation conditionally passes the index only when `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true, even though `Array.from` supplies an index for all iterable inputs.
findings.impact: Set, iterator, generator, and other iterable users get `undefined` for the mapper index despite the README and type definition promising an index. Existing tests cover non-array values but not their indexes.
evidence: index.js:107-112 computes `iterableIsArray` and passes `undefined` as the second mapper argument for non-array iterables.
readme.md:80-84 says the mapper receives item value and index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`.
index.d.ts:38-42 repeats the same `Array.from` equivalence and types the mapper's second argument as `number`.
test.js:239-255 tests Set and array-iterator inputs only for mapped values, not index delivery.
Focused probe output for mapping a Set: [{"value":"a","indexType":"undefined"},{"value":"b","indexType":"undefined"},{"value":"c","indexType":"undefined"}].
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit(2); console.log(JSON.stringify(await limit.map(new Set(['a','b','c']), (value, index) => ({value, indexType: typeof index, index}))));"

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The type check is guarded by `rejectOnClear &&`, so invalid values such as `0`, empty string, and `null` are accepted when they should fail the boolean contract.
findings.impact: Configuration mistakes are silently coerced into the default clear behavior. This weakens the runtime validation promised by the TypeScript surface and by the explicit error path for invalid `rejectOnClear` values.
evidence: index.js:12 only throws when `rejectOnClear` is both truthy and not a boolean.
index.d.ts:101-106 types `rejectOnClear` as optional boolean.
index.test-d.ts:29 expects a type error for string `rejectOnClear`, but no runtime test exercises falsey non-booleans.
Focused probe output: {"value":0,"accepted":true}; {"value":"","accepted":true}; {"value":null,"accepted":true}.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; for (const value of [0, '', null]) { try { pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: value}); console.log({value, accepted: true}); } catch (error) { console.log({value, accepted: false, name: error.name}); } }"

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is rejected even though the baseline validator accepted it
findings.cause: The validator now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency)` and removed the explicit `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` acceptance branch present in the checked-in baseline.
findings.impact: Users relying on `pLimit(Infinity)` as an unlimited concurrency mode now get a TypeError. This is a behavioral regression relative to the repository baseline, though the public README only states a minimum of 1 and does not call out Infinity explicitly.
evidence: Current index.js:127-130 requires an integer greater than 0.
`git show HEAD:index.js` shows the baseline at lines 123-125 accepted `(Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0`.
Focused probe output for `pLimit(Infinity)`: `TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; try { pLimit(Infinity); console.log('accepted'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.name + ': ' + error.message); }"
